summary: The meeting covered a proposed door-to-door solicitation ordinance. Public Portion 
 1. Amended Ordinance Chapter 279 Article VII — Door to Door Sales (09/08/2026) 
On October 13, 2026, the General Government Committee, chaired by Councilor Justin Hurst, 
met to review the proposed Door-to-Door Solicitation Ordinance, sponsored by Councilors Hurst 
and Gerry Martin. Attorney Daniel Downing outlined proposed registration requirements, 
identification cards, background checks, and an appeals process to address aggressive solicitation 
practices and resident safety. The ordinance would limit commercial solicitation to 9:00 a.m. 
through 6:00 p.m., require compliance with posted no-solicitation signs, and establish a 
voluntary Do Not Solicit Registry. Religious, political, charitable, and other noncommercial 
activities would generally remain exempt. 
 
Discussion addressed enforcement, fines, registration suspension or revocation, accountability 
for individual solicitors and businesses, and protections against repeated violations. The 
committee also considered age restrictions, constitutional concerns, consistent ordinance 
language, registry administration, and improvements to the appeals process. 
 
Councilors Hurst and Martin will seek additional community feedback and consult with the City 
Clerk and Police Department regarding implementation and enforcement. The ordinance will 
remain under unfinished business pending further review. No formal recommendation was made. 
A motion to adjourn was made, seconded by Councilor Victor Davila, and approved 
unanimously. The meeting adjourned at 5:40 p.m.
